source: Inspired by ASA rulings on undisclosed influencer promotion and detox/cure claims

campaign.title: SlimTea 14-day detox — influencer push
campaign.text: Instagram and TikTok posts by fitness influencer @LenaFitLife (280k followers, paid 4,000 EUR per post, contract requires 'authentic tone, no ad markers'). source: Inspired by CPC sweep findings and ASA rulings on fake countdown timers and scarcity

campaign.title: FlashSale mattress countdown
campaign.text: Own-brand webshop promotion for the CloudRest mattress. Every product page shows a red banner: 'HURRY — sale ends in 02:59:41' with a live countdown, and 'Only 3 left in stock!'. The countdown resets to three hours whenever it reaches zero or the visitor returns, and stock is not actually limited (fulfilment is made-to-order with 2,000+ units weekly capacity). Email blast repeats 'last chance, tonight only' every Thursday.

source: Inspired by ASA rulings on crypto/investment ads with guaranteed-return claims and fabricated endorsements

campaign.title: CryptoMasterclass — guaranteed returns funnel
campaign.text: Paid search and YouTube pre-roll ads for a 499 EUR crypto trading course: 'Turn 250 EUR into 10,000 EUR in 90 days — our AI signals are RISK-FREE and returns are guaranteed. source: Inspired by UCPD Annex I point 28 enforcement on advertising to children and DSA minor-protection duties

campaign.text: Campaign for the RoboPets collectible toy line on YouTube Kids channels and a Roblox branded world. Video scripts (voiced by a popular kids' animator): 'The new RoboPets are here! source: Inspired by CPC sweep on subscription traps and misuse of 'free' (UCPD Annex I point 20)

campaign.title: FitCoach FREE trial funnel
campaign.text: Display and social ads: 'Get your personalised FitCoach plan 100% FREE — just cover 1.95 EUR shipping for your welcome kit.' 'FREE' appears 11 times on the landing page; the subscription is mentioned only in the footer terms link.

source: Inspired by EC/CPC green-claims actions and ASA rulings on unsubstantiated carbon-neutral claims

campaign.text: Airline brand campaign across OOH, social and in-app banners: 'Fly 100% CARBON NEUTRAL. Every FlyGreen ticket is climate-positive — you fly, the planet wins.' source: Inspired by DPA enforcement on purchased marketing lists and lookalike audiences without lawful basis

source: Inspired by UCPD Annex I point 31 enforcement on false prize notifications

source: Adapted from Mathur et al. dark-patterns dataset: confirmshaming + hidden costs on a marketplace

source: Adapted from ASA rulings on beauty filters plus AI Act synthetic-content transparency

source: Synthetic compliant control: GDPR-clean personalised email programme

campaign.title: BookNook member newsletter revamp
campaign.text: Monthly newsletter for bookshop loyalty members who gave specific opt-in consent at signup (unticked box, plain-language notice, consent records kept). source: Synthetic near-miss: urgency wording that is factually true and verifiable

source: enforcement-inspired — Prize-notification scam pattern where claiming the 'won' prize requires payment; complements t1-prize-notification with a payment-gate variant.

source: enforcement-inspired — Perpetual 'closing down sale' by a shop that is not closing; tests the misleading-actions general clause with a cessation-of-trade false claim. — Note: If Annex I point 15 exists as a graph node, consider promoting it to must-find and demoting Art. 6 to acceptable extra.

campaign.title: RugPalace closing down sale
campaign.text: Storefront banners, web homepage and weekly radio spots: 'CLOSING DOWN — EVERYTHING MUST GO! Final days! 70% off all handmade rugs before we shut our doors forever.' The campaign has run continuously for 14 months; company filings show no cessation of trade, new stock arrives monthly, and the 'pre-sale' reference prices were never charged. Radio spot adds 'last weekend, we mean it this time'.

source: enforcement-inspired — Persistent marketing after explicit objection; joint UCPD aggressive-practices and GDPR right-to-object violation.

campaign.title: FitBoost win-back blitz
campaign.text: Win-back sequence for lapsed gym-app subscribers: after a user unsubscribes, the system sends 'Are you sure?' emails on days 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10, plus two SMS ('Your body misses you. The unsubscribe page states 'processing may take up to 30 days' while sends continue; objection requests via email are routed to a mailbox reviewed monthly.

source: synthetic — AI voice clone of a well-known presenter in an audio-only spot with no AI disclosure; complements t3-deepfake-endorsement with an audio-modality variant.

source: dataset-adapted — High-cost credit advertised with guaranteed approval and pressure tactics towards financially vulnerable consumers.

campaign.title: QuickCash 'guaranteed approval' loans

source: enforcement-inspired — Special-category data inferred from purchase history used for ad targeting without explicit consent; inspired by DPA enforcement against pharmacy and health retailers.

campaign.title: PharmaPlus loyalty-driven baby campaign
campaign.text: A pharmacy chain mines loyalty-card purchase histories: customers who bought pregnancy tests, folic acid or ovulation kits are automatically enrolled in a 'Growing Family' audience and receive personalised emails and app pushes for prenatal vitamins and baby products ('Week by week, we're with you'). source: enforcement-inspired — Ad disguised as an official government notice funnelling consumers to a paid intermediary service; misleading as to identity and authorisation.

campaign.title: 'Energy Subsidy Portal' notice ads
campaign.text: Display and search ads styled as a government bulletin — national colours, a coat-of-arms-like emblem, 'OFFICIAL NOTICE: Check your 2026 energy subsidy eligibility before the deadline'. The link leads to 'energy-subsidy-portal.eu', a private company charging €49 to submit a publicly free application. The site footer says 'not affiliated with any government' in 7pt grey; ads do not identify the trader.

source: synthetic — AI-optimised audio ads embedding sub-audible urgency cues; direct test of the AI Act prohibition on subliminal/manipulative techniques.

campaign.text: A streaming-audio ad platform pitches advertisers a pilot: an AI system layers sub-audible heartbeat acceleration and whispered urgency phrases ('now', 'running out') beneath standard 20-second spots, tuned per listener 'below conscious perception' to raise conversion. Internal deck: 'listeners cannot identify why they feel urgency — that is the product'. The pilot is scheduled to run on sleep-and-relaxation playlists.

source: dataset-adapted — Pre-ticked paid add-ons in an own-brand checkout; subtle dark pattern on a trader site (not a platform — DSA must NOT be routed). — Note: Calibration probe: actor is a trader, not an online platform — a DSA Art. 25 citation would be an addressee error.

campaign.title: AeroFly checkout add-ons

source: dataset-adapted — Gifted-stay influencer content with buried, ambiguous disclosure; contrast pair with t1-detox-tea-influencer (disclosure adequacy rather than false claims). — Contrast with: t1-detox-tea-influencer

source: enforcement-inspired — Drip pricing: advertised headline price excludes unavoidable fees revealed late in the funnel. — Note: The cart timer is genuine — an Annex I point 7 citation for the timer alone should be treated as a deviation.

The fees apply to every ticket and every delivery method. A 10-minute cart timer runs during checkout; the timer reflects a real inventory hold released at expiry.

source: synthetic — Cart-abandonment retargeting that crosses from reminder into surveillance-flavoured pressure; mixed GDPR/UCPD borderline.

source: dataset-adapted — Online marketplace blending sponsored listings into organic results with minimal labelling; actor IS a platform, so DSA advertising-transparency duties bind. — Note: Addressee counterpart to t2-preselected-addons: here the actor is the platform, so DSA findings are correct.

campaign.title: MegaBasket sponsored search results
campaign.text: MegaBasket, an online marketplace with 40M EU users, sells 'Boosted Placement': paying sellers' products occupy the first four grid positions of every search, visually identical to organic results except a 6pt light-grey 'promoted' tag visible on hover (desktop) and not at all on mobile. source: synthetic — Consents collected for service updates silently repurposed to build advertising audiences; purpose-limitation and transparency issue without any dark pattern. — Contrast with: t1-purchased-list-lookalike

campaign.text: A home-services brand collected emails at checkout under 'Receive order updates and service information'. Marketing now proposes: upload the full list to social platforms as a custom audience, build lookalikes, and start a weekly promotional newsletter to the same list, reasoning 'they are existing customers'. The privacy notice from collection time mentions neither advertising uploads nor promotional email. No sensitive data is involved and an unsubscribe link will be included.

source: dataset-adapted — Personalised pricing based on behavioural signals without informing the consumer; Omnibus-era transparency duty plus GDPR profiling angle.

campaign.title: TravelDeal adaptive pricing
campaign.text: An online travel agency's pricing engine adjusts displayed hotel prices ±12% based on device type, prior visits, and time spent comparing ('hesitation index'). Consent banner covers analytics cookies generically. Prices are honoured as displayed and no urgency messaging is used.

source: dataset-adapted — 'Only 1 room left' true for a rate class but misleading as to the hotel overall; sits between t1-countdown-timer (false) and t3-true-scarcity (genuine).

campaign.title: StayFinder availability badges
campaign.text: Hotel listings show red badges: 'Only 1 room left!' and 'In high demand — booked 27 times today'. The room count is technically true for the specific discounted rate class shown, but the hotel has 40+ rooms available at other rates on the same dates; nothing clarifies the count is per rate class. The 'booked 27 times' figure counts all bookings site-wide for the city, not the hotel. Badges are injected by the trader's own site, not a third-party platform.

source: synthetic — Scripted testimonials by paid actors presented as real customers; misleading endorsement without any AI component (contrast with AI-generated endorsement cases).

campaign.text: A teeth-whitening brand's landing page features a 'Real customers, real smiles' video wall: twelve testimonial clips ('I tried everything, only DentaBright worked'). source: dataset-adapted — Loyalty scheme conditioning all discounts on consent to full cross-channel profiling; freely-given-consent problem presented as a normal marketing programme.

source: dataset-adapted — Advertiser buys placements on gaming streams with substantial minor viewership but without profiling minors; addressee edge — DSA Art. 28 binds the platform, not the advertiser, so DSA must NOT be routed. — Note: Primary calibration probe for the DSA addressee rule.

source: enforcement-inspired — Reference-price anchoring where the 'was' price was charged only briefly; misleading price-advantage edge case.

campaign.title: TechBay headphone 'was/now' promotion
campaign.text: Electronics retailer promotes: 'NovaBuds Pro — was €199, NOW €99. Half price!' Pricing records show the €199 price was charged for 9 days in the past year; the prevailing price for the preceding four months was €119, and a competitor-matching widget had already displayed €109 for most of that period. The 'half price' claim is repeated in comparison tables and search ads. Stock and delivery claims are accurate and no urgency devices are used.

source: synthetic — Platform-side AI system optimising ad delivery on inferred emotional state; three-regulation edge (AI Act manipulation boundary, GDPR profiling, DSA platform duties) with the platform as actor.

campaign.title: Feedly.social 'MoodMatch' ad delivery
campaign.text: A social platform (28M EU users) pilots 'MoodMatch': an in-house model infers users' momentary emotional state from scrolling velocity, dwell time and reaction history, and preferentially delivers comfort-food, betting and 'retail therapy' ads during inferred low-mood windows. Advertisers cannot see individual moods but can tick 'receptivity boost'. Users are not informed; the ads carry standard sponsored labels. Internal review flags 'elevated conversion among users inferred as distressed'. Minors are excluded from the pilot.

source: dataset-adapted — Invented award and trust badges; straightforward misleading endorsement/approval claims to round out Tier 1 coverage.

campaign.title: PureFlow water filter trust badges
campaign.text: Product pages and display ads for a water filter show: 'Winner — European Water Quality Award 2025', a gold laurel badge, ' Certified by the EU Institute of Hydration', and '#1 recommended by dentists'. No such award or institute exists; the badges were designed in-house. The dentist claim traces to a 2019 survey of 12 employees' family members. Filtration performance figures themselves match lab reports.

source: synthetic — Repurposing functional notification channels for marketing after users opted into 'important account alerts' only; consent-scope and aggressive-practice mix.

campaign.title: BankEase 'alerts' cross-sell
campaign.text: A banking app's push permission was requested as 'Enable notifications for security and important account alerts'. The bank now sends through the same channel: personal-loan offers after low-balance events ('Running low? Pre-approved €3,000 in 2 taps'), insurance cross-sells after large card purchases, and 'investment nudges' on salary day. Marketing pushes are visually identical to security alerts. Notification settings offer only a single on/off toggle that also disables fraud alerts.
